messages:
Jules (docs): Quick thread: doing a pass over Dedicated provisioning docs. Found mixed terminology in examples (reserved_pool vs reservedCapacity), a dangling include that points to an old anchor, and one SDK snippet using ClientV1. I'd like to open a single PR that: 1) normalizes field names to reserved_capacity, 2) fixes the anchor + adds a redirect, 3) updates SDK snippets to v2 and adds a brief migration table. Thoughts?

link-bot: Automated scan: 4 files with deprecated tokens, 1 broken include reference. Report: https://ci.internal/doc-scans/5032109876

Omar (eng): Sounds good. We standardized on reserved_capacity in the runtime a while ago. Recommend also adding a one-liner explaining reserved_capacity vs dedicated_reservation to avoid confusion with billing terms.

Jules (docs): Good call. Draft one-liner: "reserved_capacity (config) specifies the pool of GPU slots reserved for a tenant; it is distinct from billing 'dedicated_reservation' which is the contractual commit." Keep it short?

Tasha (product): Yes, that will help support calls. Also please include an SLA note that reserved_capacity changes may take up to 5 minutes to fully provision during peak hours. Short line under 'Provisioning timeline'.

Lee (infra): I'll own the anchor redirect in infra-docs. If you give me the old id I can add an HTML redirect and a 301 in the static includes.

Jules (docs): Old anchor id is #reserved-pools-usage. Also one include references #isolation-labels-old which no longer exists. I'll update the include to the new section id.

Omar (eng): For the SDK snippet: please use ProvisioningClient from redwood-sdk v2. Also update method names: create_tenant_reserved_capacity -> tenants.create_reserved_capacity. Provide both a minimal Python and TS snippet for copy-paste.

Jules (docs): Draft Python v2 snippet: ```python
# redwood-sdk v2
from redwood import ProvisioningClient
client = ProvisioningClient()
payload = {"reserved_capacity": {"gpus": 4, "region": "us-west-2"}}
client.tenants.create_reserved_capacity("t-99", payload)
```
Draft TS one-liner: `await client.tenants.createReservedCapacity("t-99", payload)`

Tasha (product): Also add a tiny example showing how reserved_capacity interacts with autoscale: if reserved_capacity > 0 and scalePolicy.min_instances < reserved_capacity then reserved_capacity will be honored. Maybe a note: "min_instances should be >= reserved_capacity to guarantee capacity is always kept warm."

Lee (infra): I'll add the redirect PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra-docs/pull/999 — will reference your docs PR once opened.

Jules (docs): Migration table (one-line rows): "ClientV1 -> ProvisioningClient (v2)", "autoscale -> scalePolicy", "reserved_pool -> reserved_capacity". I'll add these under a 'Quick migration' box.

Omar (eng): Minor nit: change method name in Python snippet to `create_reserved_capacity` (snake_case) and TS to `createReservedCapacity` (camelCase) to match SDK patterns. Also remove hardcoded tenant IDs in examples and note to replace with real tenant.

Jules (docs): Updated snippets and removed hardcoded API keys. Also added CLI sample: `rwctl tenants reserve --tenant $TENANT_ID --gpus 4 --region us-west-2`.

link-bot: Scheduled re-scan after linked PRs merge.

Tasha (product): I'll run a staging smoke once merged. Please add a test checklist item in the PR: "apply reservation to staging tenant, verify reserved instances count and that autoscale respects min_instances."

Jules (docs): Will include checklist and link to staging runbook. Opening docs PR now: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/5012 — includes anchor fixes, migration table, updated examples, CLI and SDK snippets, and a one-line SLA note.

Lee (infra): Redirect PR linked in your PR comments.

Omar (eng): Quick review done, left 2 tiny wording nits.

Jules (docs): Addressed the nits and pushed. Thanks everyone. Closing thread after successful merge and re-scan.
